title: US equity markets close early at 1:00 p.m. ET — the day after Thanksgiving 2028, the second of the year's two early closes and the furthest-out event on this calendar
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this lane (HTTP 200 after its 302 — the page needs curl -L — 109,180 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell; all 133 'text' cells read, the holiday grid recovered as 10 four-column rows (Holiday / 2026 / 2027 / 2028) and every footnote read whole. The page states 'All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028'; its Thanksgiving Day row gives 'Thursday, November 23***' in the 2028 column, and footnote *** reads verbatim: 'Each market will close early at 1:00 p.m. (1:15 p.m. for eligible options) on Friday, November 27, 2026, Friday, November 26, 2027, and Friday, November 24, 2028 (the day after Thanksgiving). NYSE American Equities, NYSE Arca Equities, NYSE National, and NYSE Texas late trading sessions will close at 5:00 p.m. All times are Eastern Time.' The 2028 date is READ from the footnote, not derived from the Thursday. Independently reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Thanksgiving on the FOURTH Thursday in November, the fourth Thursday of November 2028 is 2028-11-23, and the day after is Friday 2028-11-24. BOND SIDE NOT CLAIMABLE FOR 2028, unlike the 2027 sibling: sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule re-fetched the same session (HTTP 200, 299,159 bytes) and its RSC payload unescaped and searched in full carries US holiday cards for 2026 and 2027 only — its Thanksgiving cards name 2026-11-27 and 2027-11-26 with an 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time)' each, and the string '2028' appears just 5 times, every one of them inside a 'New Year's Day 2027/2028' heading and none in a holiday row. SIFMA publishes two years forward where NYSE publishes three, so no fixed-income recommendation for 2028-11-24 is asserted. OPTIONS SIDE ALSO UNSOURCED: cboe.com/about/hours/us-options/ (HTTP 200, 386,116 bytes) contains the string '2028' zero times. Filed estimate on the same two counts every sibling half-day entry documents (thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27, thanksgiving-half-day-2027-11-26): the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs has no slot for an exchange operator's own hours page (open issue #2552), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: CANONICAL file written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), promoting proposals/thanksgiving-half-day-2028-11-24.from-presidential-election-2028-11-07.json per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md; the proposal is now shadowed and stays where it is. Schema follows thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 and -2027-11-26 exactly — kind 'sector', impact low, symbols [], estimate with a NEWS: source — and invents no new kind. WHAT THIS INSTANCE ADDS THAT ITS TWO SIBLINGS DO NOT, and the reason it is not transcription: the 2026 ledger tested four folk seasonals against ORDINARY-FRIDAY base rates and left exactly one standing (VIX rises on 18 of 33 day-after-Thanksgiving Fridays, 54.5% vs a 36.4% Friday base, p = 0.025); the 2027 ledger generalised it to a POST-HOLIDAY rebound (213/302 at 70.5% vs a 45.6% weekday-matched base) and recorded that it could not tell repricing from a marking artifact off daily bars. This session resolved the dose question both siblings left open and the answer RETIRES the anomaly: the non-return component of the VIX change is a monotone function of CALENDAR DAYS ELAPSED since the previous session, not of holidays. Controlling for the session's own SPY return, each extra calendar day the market is shut adds 0.254 VIX points (t = 20.2, n = 8,459 sessions 1993-2025), and the raw residual buckets run -0.113 (1 day) / +0.323 (2 days) / +0.359 (3 days) / +0.770 (4 days). The day after Thanksgiving is a TWO-calendar-day reopening, and against other two-calendar-day reopenings it is dead on the null: VIX up 18/33 (54.5%) vs 26/47 (55.3%), P = 0.61. An ordinary MONDAY, a three-calendar-day reopening, runs hotter at 61.1%. So the correct base rate for 2028-11-24 is ~55%, not the 36% ordinary-Friday base that made it look anomalous in 2026 and not the 70.7% pooled post-holiday rate that overstates it. WHAT STAYS TRUE AND THANKSGIVING-SPECIFIC IS THE THINNESS, which is a half-session effect and not a dose effect: SPY volume median 0.429x its trailing-20 median against 0.797x for other two-calendar-day reopenings and 0.883x for ordinary Mondays. 2028 STRUCTURE, read from the same NYSE grid: 2028 has NINE NYSE holidays rather than ten, because New Year's Day 2028 falls on a Saturday and footnote * says no holiday is observed; and it has TWO early closes, Monday July 3 2028 (footnote **, proposed in this PR as independence-day-half-day-2028-07-03) and this one — so unlike 2027, which had exactly one, this instance has a rehearsal five months ahead of it. Christmas Day 2028 is a Monday and carries no early-close footnote. Impact is LOW and symbols is empty: this is a market-structure fact that changes how other events are READ, not an event with its own directional content. Estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
